title: Sparse Table: Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA)
statement:
Given a rooted tree with N nodes (root = 1) and Q queries, find the Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA) of nodes u and v for each query.

Use binary lifting (a sparse table on ancestors) to answer each LCA query in O(log N) after O(N log N) preprocessing.

The tree is given as N-1 undirected edges.
inputFormat:
The first line contains N and Q.
The next N-1 lines each contain two integers u and v (an undirected edge).
The next Q lines each contain u and v (an LCA query).
outputFormat: Q lines, each the LCA of the queried pair.

examples.explanation: Tree: 1-(2,3), 2-(4,5), 3-(6,7). LCA(4,5)=2. LCA(4,7)=1. LCA(2,6)=3 (2's path: 2->1, 6's path: 6->3->1, LCA=1 ? No: LCA(2,6)=1 since 2 is under 1, and 6 is under 3 under 1. Actually LCA(2,6)=1).
